findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple cold held temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods in the open air cooler to have an internal temperature above 41F:
1) Hard boiled eggs had an ambient temperature of 51F, and probed at 45F. Three total packages of hard boiled eggs (two were in compliance) were probed for internal temperatures and voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC). 
2) Two containers of Chobani yogurt were probed and one had an internal temperatures of 45F (the other had an internal temperature that was in compliance). Both containers were voluntarily discarded by the PIC.
3) Egg and dill salad sandwich and carrot cake had ambient temperatures of 48F. When probed they had internal temperature that were in compliance, however were discarded to be probed.
CORRECTED- probed items were discarded, and items in the open air cooler were pushed backwards. Ambient thermometers in the cooling unit show proper cold holding temperatures. Ensure all TCS items are monitored to be cold holding at 41F or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Manager washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed, and educational poster on proper technique was provided. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
**To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11 Stem of the digital food thermometer was soiled with food debris. Stem was cleaned during inspection. Use and general maintenance of food thermometer were discussed. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes are used during prep, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.
--F'real machines were observed with dried food splash on surfaces where shakes and smoothies are mixed. Manager noted the entire machine has a cleaning process that occurs up to every 24hrs or it doesn't work. The surfaces that are visible and can be accessed, such as the mixing wand/area around it where splash occurs, need to be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use since they come in contact with time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food.
Food contact surfaces of equipment used with TCS foods shall be cleaned up to every 4hrs after continuous use. 
--Nozzles and diffusers of soda machines had varying amounts of mold buildup. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12 Dried food splash was observed in the microwaves. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Tube at creamer dispenser was observed to be cut straight across and holding a portion of product at room temperature in the bottom of the tip where creamer dispenses into customer cups. Manger cut the tubes at more of an angle to allow for proper draining between uses. Ensure all staff are properly trained and that tubes for creamer are cut at an angle to avoid the issue of ponding creamer in the bottom of tubes at room temperature between uses.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.
